cards.text: Job has been answering his friends (Job 12:1-13:19), and now he turns and talks straight to God. Before anything else, he asks God for two things. Grant those, Job says, and he won't need to hide from Him.

cards.question: Job asks God for two things so he won't have to hide. What are they?

answers.text: Take His hand off Job and don't terrify him
Heal Job's sores and bring back his flocks
Quiet Job's friends and send Job a sign

cards.question: Once God grants those two things, what does Job want from Him?

answers.text: A chance to talk it out together
A promise to restore all he lost
A sign that his friends are mistaken

cards.text: Then Job asks God to reveal something to him. No hints. No riddles. No "you'll figure it out." Just SHOW me.

cards.question: Job asks God to show him his ___.

cards.text: Then comes the hard question. Job asks God, "Why do You hide Your face and consider me as Your enemy?"

cards.question: Job asks God if He would frighten a windblown leaf or chase after dry chaff. What is Job saying about himself?

answers.text: He's too weak to be worth chasing
He's ready to blow away somewhere new
He's sure to grow back next season

cards.text: Job's not done. He says God writes down bitter accusations against him. I think Job feels like he's standing under a spotlight while somebody takes NOTES.

cards.question: True or false: Job says God hands him the iniquities of his youth.

cards.text: Then Job says God puts his feet in the stocks and keeps watch over every path he takes. Locked in one spot? Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, I know STUCK.

cards.question: Job ends the thought with a picture of a garment the moths have gotten into. What is he saying about man?

answers.text: He slowly wears out and falls apart
He looks fine but hides a stain
He's easy to swap out for another

cards.text: Then Job talks about every person ever born of a woman. Kings, cashiers, the guy who hits reply-all on the whole office. EVERYBODY.

cards.question: True or false: Job says a person's life is long but full of trouble.

cards.text: To show what he means, Job grabs a picture anybody can see just by stepping outside.

cards.question: Job says a person comes up like a flower and then ___.

cards.text: He's like a fleeting shadow too, here and then GONE, like a fresh batch on my cooling rack the second I turn my back. Then Job asks God if He really fixes His eyes on someone like that and brings him into judgment.

cards.question: True or false: Job says anyone who tries hard enough can bring something clean out of something unclean.

cards.text: Job says God has numbered a man's days and set limits he can't go past. Like a parking meter that's already set, and you can't feed it ONE more minute.

cards.question: Since God has already set those limits on a man's days, what does Job ask Him to do?

answers.text: Look away and let him rest
Add more days to his life
Show him the day he will die

cards.text: Let him rest, Job says, so he can enjoy his day like a hired hand. That's the worker watching the clock, friend, just waiting to clock out and finally put those feet up.
Then Job looks at a TREE. Picture it chopped down to a stump, its roots getting old in the ground.

cards.question: What does Job say happens to a tree that's been cut down?
Even if the tree's roots grow old and its stump dies in the soil, what makes it bud again?

cards.text: Then Job turns to a man. "But a man dies and is laid low; he breathes his last, and where is he?"
It's like water disappearing from the sea, Job says, or a river drying up. Not "be right back." GONE.

cards.question: True or false: Job says a man who lies down in death rises again just like the tree.

cards.text: Then Job says, "If only You would hide me in Sheol and conceal me until Your anger has passed!"

cards.question: Job asks God to hide him in Sheol. After that, what does Job ask God to do?

answers.text: Set a time and remember him
Heal every one of his sores
Send someone else to bring him out

cards.text: Hide me, then remember me? Friend, that was the drawer, except NOBODY set a timer for me. Then Job asks the big one: "When a man dies, will he live again?"

cards.question: Through all the days of his hard service, Job says he will ___ until his renewal comes.
True or false: Job pictures a day when God calls, Job answers, and God longs for the work of His hands.
On that day, Job says, God would count his steps but would not keep track of his ___.

cards.text: Then Job grabs a picture for it: his transgression sealed up in a bag. Sealed TIGHT, like a cookie box I just finished taping shut.

cards.question: Job pictures his transgression sealed in a bag. What does he say God would do with his iniquity?

cards.text: Then Job says a mountain crumbles and water wears away the stones. Slow, friend. Like one tiny crack in your phone screen that creeps a little farther EVERY. SINGLE. DAY.

cards.question: Job says water wears away stone. What does he say God does in the same way?

cards.text: Job says God overpowers a man, and he passes on. God changes his face and sends him away. Heavy stuff, friend. Job doesn't soften a single word of it.

cards.question: True or false: Job says a man who has passed on still knows when his sons are honored.
Job ends by saying a man feels only the pain of his own ___.

cards.text: And that's where Job stops talking, for now. Stick around, friend, because this conversation is FAR from over.

findings.problem: The setup says only that Job wants God to reveal something. The earlier cards give the baker no basis for reasoning out 'sins' rather than 'future' or 'purpose,' so the blank tests wording the baker has not seen.
